arxiv-2108-09848.title: CoMet: Modeling Group Cohesion for Socially Compliant Robot Navigation in Crowded Scenes
arxiv-2108-09848.creator: Adarsh Jagan Sathyamoorthy, Utsav Patel, Moumita Paul, Nithish K Sanjeev Kumar, Yash Savle
arxiv-2108-09848.description: Abstract We present CoMet, a novel approach for computing a group’s cohesion and using that to improve a robot’s navigation in crowded scenes. Our approach uses a novel cohesion-metric that builds on prior work in social psychology. We compute this metric by utilizing various visual features of pedestrians from an RGB-D camera on-board a robot.

arxiv-2111-14286.title: Analyzing polarized boosted top from stop decay at high luminosity and high energy LHC
arxiv-2111-14286.creator: Jayita Lahiri
arxiv-2111-14286.description: Abstract Measuring top polarization is extremely important in understanding any new physics that couples to top quark. Here, we take up the task of extracting polarization of top quark coming from TeV-scale stop decay at the upgraded high luminosity and high energy LHC.

arxiv-2210-03107.title: AdS/BCFT from Conformal Bootstrap:
arxiv-2210-03107.creator: Construction of Gravity with Branes and Particles
arxiv-2210-03107.description: Abstract We initiate a conformal bootstrap program to study AdS 3 /BCFT 2 with heavy excitations. We start by solving the bootstrap equations associated with two-point functions of scalar/non-scalar primaries under the assumption that one-point functions vanish. These correspond to gravity with a brane and a non-spinning/spinning particle where the brane and the particle do not intersect with each other.

arxiv-2411-18603.title: Modular invariant inflation and reheating
arxiv-2411-18603.creator: Gui-Jun Ding, Si-Yi Jiang, Yong Xu, Wenbin Zhao
arxiv-2411-18603.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gui-Jun Ding, Si-Yi Jiang, Yong Xu, Wenbin Zhao. We use modular symmetry as an organizing principle that attempts to simultaneously address the lepton flavor puzzle, inflation, and post-inflationary reheating. We demonstrate this approach using the finite modular group A 4 A_{4} in the lepton sector. In our model, neutrino masses are generated via the Type-I see-saw mechanism, with modular symmetry dictating the form of the Yukawa couplings and right-handed neutrino masses.

arxiv-2504-00498.title: Dynamical Similarity in Higher - Order Classical Symplectic Systems
arxiv-2504-00498.creator: Callum Bell, David Sloan
arxiv-2504-00498.description: Abstract Many theories of physical interest, which admit a Hamiltonian description, exhibit symmetries under a particular class of non - strictly canonical transformation, known as dynamical similarities. The presence of such symmetries allows a reduction process to be carried out, eliminating a single degree of freedom from the system, which we associate with an overall scale.

arxiv-2511-13650.description: Abstract We present JWST observations of the radio galaxy TGSSJ1530+1049, spectroscopically confirmed at z = 4.0 z=4.0 . NIRCam images and NIRSpec/IFU spectroscopy ( R = 2700 R=2700 ) show that TGSSJ1530 + + 1049 is part of one of the densest-known structures of continuum and line-emitting objects found at these redshifts.

arxiv-2512-08037.creator: Justin F. Niedermeyer, Nathan K. Lysne, Katherine C. McCormick, Jonas Keller, Craig W. Hogle, Matthew G. Blain, Edwin J. Heller, Roman Schmied, Robert Jördens, Susanna L. Todaro, David J. Wineland, Andrew C. Wilson, Daniel H. Slichter, Dietrich Leibfried
arxiv-2512-08037.description: Abstract \unnumbered 1 Summary Paragraph Controlled quantum mechanical motion of trapped atomic ions can be used to simulate and explore collective quantum phenomena 32 ; 31 and to process quantum information 11 . Groups of cold atomic ions in an externally applied trapping potential self-organize into “Coulomb crystals” due to their mutual electrostatic repulsion 13 ; 43 ; 14 .

pmc-11546730.title: Monocyte Count as a Predictor of Major Adverse Limb Events in Aortoiliac Revascularization
pmc-11546730.creator: António Pereira-Neves, Lara Dias, Mariana Fragão-Marques, José Vidoedo, Hugo Ribeiro, José Paulo Andrade, João Rocha-Neves, Carlo Setacci
pmc-11546730.description: Background/Objectives: Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of death, especially in the developed world, and is marked by chronic arterial inflammation and lipid accumulation. As key players in its progression, monocytes contribute to plaque formation, inflammation, and tissue repair. Understanding monocyte involvement is crucial for developing better therapeutic approaches.

pmc-12828330.title: The effects of doxorubicin on blood-brain barrier integrity in hCMEC/D3
pmc-12828330.creator: Chadni Patel, Christina Glytsou, Mi-Hyeon Jang, Peter D. Cole
pmc-12828330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Current chemotherapy regimens have significantly improved overall survival for children with cancer. However, these treatments are associated with detrimental side effects like chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment (CICI), or “chemobrain.” Measurable deficits in cognitive function persist years after treatment. Specifically, doxorubicin (DOXO), a commonly used chemotherapeutic agent in curative regimens for children with cancer, plays a pivotal role in the development of CICI, even though it doesn’t cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB).

pmc-13378991.title: Exploring administrative staff’s acceptance of generative AI in Chinese vocational colleges: A UTAUT-guided thematic study
pmc-13378991.creator: Yangzi Zhang, Yuanyuan Tian, Kenny S. L. Cheah, Wen Fen Beh
pmc-13378991.description: As Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) technologies reshape institutional processes, higher vocational colleges are increasingly exploring their potential in administrative management. Guided by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), this qualitative study examines how administrative personnel perceive and accept GenAI in vocational college administration.

pmc-13443707.title: Application of Digital Techniques for the Observation and Fabrication of Removable Partial Dentures
pmc-13443707.creator: Su Wu, Ting Pan, Zhaohan Du, Xinman Song, Shaohai Wang
pmc-13443707.description: This study explores digital fabrication of removable partial dentures (RPD) via direct intraoral model observation. At initial diagnosis, the three‐dimensional design scheme is obtained directly by visualizing the digital model using an intraoral scanner and a three‐dimensional management platform software. This framework supports tooth preparation, data acquisition, digital chair‐side observations, and RPD design and fabrication. 1.

pmc-13586505.title: Endovascular salvage of a dislodged renal bridging stent using balloon-induced foreshortening following thoracoabdominal multibranch endograft
pmc-13586505.creator: Mark W. Mewissen, Safoora Choudry
pmc-13586505.description: A 69-year-old man underwent thoracoabdominal multibranch endograft repair. Ten days later, computed tomography angiography demonstrated type III endoleak caused by the complete dislodgement of the left renal bridging stent. During brachial reintervention, controlled balloon dilation foreshortened the displaced stent, restoring alignment with the renal artery and enabling successful reconstruction.

pmc-13656480.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses reveal phytohormone signaling mechanisms underlying differential regeneration potential in microspore-derived calli from hulled and hulless barley
pmc-13656480.creator: Runhong Gao, Guimei Guo, Yingjie Zong, Wenqi Zhang, Longhua Zhou, Hongwei Xu, Yingbo Li, Chenghong Liu
pmc-13656480.description: BackgroundIsolated microspore culture (IMC) is an effective model for investigating plant cell totipotency and is widely used in plant breeding programs to rapidly produce doubled haploid lines. However, the limited regeneration capacity of hulless barely restricts the broader application of IMC in breeding improvement and research.

pmc-13682908.title: Predicting Major Amputation Rates in Diabetic Hindfoot Ulcers With Critical Infection and Ischemia: A Risk-Factor-Based Model
pmc-13682908.creator: Kyu-Il Lee, Woo-Sung Kim, Seung-Kyu Han, Kyung-Chul Moon, Sik Namgoong, Seong-Ho Jeong, Eun-Sang Dhong
pmc-13682908.description: BackgroundDiabetic hindfoot ulcers pose a substantially greater risk of progressing to major amputation than forefoot or midfoot ulcers. Patients with these ulcers often experience severe psychological distress at the prospect of major limb loss. Consequently, patients, their families, and healthcare professionals prioritize understanding the actual risk of major amputation based on the patient’s current clinical status.

pmc-13693241.title: Alternative life history strategies of a marine parasitic dinoflagellate
pmc-13693241.creator: Xuqing Chen, Kimberly S Reece, Sebastian G Gornik, Jeffrey D Shields
pmc-13693241.description: BackgroundAs adaptive organisms, parasites display remarkable diversity in their life cycles and life history strategies, reflecting evolutionary pressures to find and inhabit their hosts. The order Syndiniales (i.e., Marine Alveolates II and IV) has been detected in global waters and has gained increasing interest in metabarcoding studies as cryptic members of the plankton.

uslaw-usc-t42-s7701.title: 42 U.S.C. § 7701 — Congressional findings
uslaw-usc-t42-s7701.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s7701.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 86 (Earthquake Hazards Reduction). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Congress finds and declares the following: (1) All 50 States, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, are vulnerable to the hazards of earthquakes, and at least 39 of them are subject to major or moderate seismic risk, including Alaska, California, Hawaii.
